VANCOUVER, BRITISH COLUMBIA – NOVEMBER 13th, 2026 –– TheNewswire - HYPER BIT TECHNOLOGIES LTD. (CSE: HYPE) (OTC: HYPAF) (FWB: N7S0) (the “Company”, “Hyper Bit”, or “HYPE”) is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Yoshito Okubo as Chief Executive Officer as well as the addition of Mr. Cole Drezdoff to the board of directors effective immediately. These strategic changes and addition to the Hyper Bit board add significant depth and experience within the digital assets and artificial intelligence “AI” sectors.

 

"We are pleased to welcome Mr. Drezdoff to Hyper Bit’s Board as we advance existing crypto mining operations and evaluate new opportunities across digital assets and AI infrastructure,” said Yoshito Okubo, CEO and a director of Hyper Bit. “Mr. Drezdoff brings a commercially focused perspective and experience in business development, digital marketing and stakeholder communications. His skills will strengthen our team as we refine our strategy, build relationships and communicate our progress to shareholders.”

 

Mr. Drezdoff is a commercially focused marketing and business development professional with experience in digital asset strategies, technology and AI market research, investor engagement and client growth initiatives. He developed an early interest in emerging blockchain technologies and digital assets, becoming involved in the cryptocurrency space in 2016. A graduate of Toronto Metropolitan University's Ted Rogers School of Management with a Bachelor of Commerce in Marketing Management, he has supported companies in strengthening brand visibility, improving stakeholder communications and driving business development. His experience spans digital marketing, social media, lead generation, operations, client engagement and financial communications, giving him a practical, entrepreneurial approach to helping businesses execute growth strategies and expand commercial opportunities.

About Hyper Bit Technologies Ltd.

 

Hyper Bit Technologies Ltd. is a forward-thinking, diversified technology company specializing in the acquisition, development, and strategic deployment of crypto mining operations and blockchain-based innovations. As global interest in digital assets accelerates—driven by the rise of blockchain, decentralized finance (DeFi), and increasing institutional and retail adoption—Hyper Bit is committed to unlocking value across the crypto ecosystem while delivering growth for our stakeholders. Hyper Bit Technologies Ltd. is a member of the Blockchain Association of Canada and the American Blockchain & Cryptocurrency Association.

 

Stay informed on our latest developments by subscribing to Company updates at Hyperbit.ca and follow us across our social media channels: X.com, TikTok, Instagram, and LinkedIn. Hyper Bit Technologies Ltd. is publicly listed in Canada (CSE: HYPE), the USA (OTC: HYPAF) and in Europe (FWB: N7S0).

FDA Fast Track Designation for Plinabulin plus docetaxel marks key regulatory milestone in DUBLIN-4 study population of Post-ICI Non-Squamous NSCLC with no actionable genomic alteration (AGA)

Strategic transaction with Biolin provides data from approximately half of DUBLIN-4’s 442 patients and supports the planned interim analysis at 221 PFS events

FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BeyondSpring Inc. (NASDAQ: BYSI) (“BeyondSpring” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage company developing innovative therapies for the treatment of cancer and other diseases, today announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a corporate update highlighting regulatory and strategic progress for Plinabulin and its global Phase 3 DUBLIN-4 trial.

“The third quarter marked an important regulatory and strategic step forward for Plinabulin,” said Min Qiu, Chief Executive Officer of BeyondSpring. “The FDA’s Fast Track designation underscores the significant unmet need for new treatment options for NSCLC patients without AGA and progressing after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, where docetaxel is still the standard of care.  Plinabulin has been shown to improve the tolerability and dose intensity of docetaxel and demonstrated a long-term survival benefit in the previous successful DUBLIN-3 study in second- and third-line EGFR wild-type NSCLC, published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine in 2024.”

Mr. Qiu continued, “With an FDA-aligned Phase 3 design and a strategic transaction with Biolin to support approximately half of DUBLIN-4’s planned 442-patient enrollment, generating quality data from China, we remain focused on advancing the study toward its prespecified interim analysis at 221 progression-free survival events. We believe positive interim results could represent a significant value inflection point for BeyondSpring, as we continue to pursue financing and strategic opportunities to support global execution.”

Recent Regulatory, Clinical and Corporate Highlights

FDA Fast Track designation for Plinabulin plus docetaxel in post-ICI non-squamous NSCLC

  • The Company announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted Fast Track designation to Plinabulin plus docetaxel for advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable genomic alterations (AGA), following prior anti-PD-(L)1 therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy.
  • The designated population corresponds to the second- or third-line patient population targeted in the global DUBLIN-4 trial. Fast Track designation may facilitate more frequent FDA interactions and, if applicable criteria are met, rolling review of a future application.

Strategic transaction to fund half of DUBLIN-4’s planned patient enrollment

  • The Company completed the sale of BeyondSpring Ltd., its wholly owned subsidiary that indirectly held the majority equity interest in Dalian Wanchunbulin Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (“Bulin”), to Biolin Investment Limited (“Biolin”) on September 30, 2026, pursuant to a definitive agreement among the parties.
  • As non-cash consideration, Biolin will support the funding of DUBLIN-4 clinical development activities conducted by Bulin at participating sites in China, which are expected to include enrollment of approximately 221 patients, or approximately half of the planned 442-patient global enrollment. BeyondSpring will receive access to clinical data generated from the China portion of the trial.

Third Quarter Financial Results

Continuing operations:

  • Research and development (R&D) expenses were $1.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.1 million was primarily due to a $0.3 million increase in preclinical expenses related to Plinabulin treatment combination research in support of strategic business development and partnership initiatives, partially offset by lower patent-related legal services and drug manufacturing costs.
  • General and administrative (G&A) expenses were $1.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $0.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.3 million was primarily due to an increase in legal fees related to financing activities and higher consulting expenses related to accounting advisory and audit services, partially offset by lower personnel-related and travel expenses.
  • Net loss was $2.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
  • Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments were $0.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $4.0 million as of December 31, 2025.

Year-to-Date Financial Results

Continuing operations:

  • Research and development (R&D) expenses were $3.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.4 million was primarily due to expanded drug manufacturing activities and increased preclinical Plinabulin treatment combination research, partially offset by lower patent-related legal services and personnel-related expenses.
  • General and administrative (G&A) expenses were $2.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease of $0.5 million was primarily due to lower personnel-related expenses, mainly from lower incentive compensation and share-based compensation, as well as lower professional service expenses in legal advisory and lower travel and entertainment expenses.
  • Net loss was $5.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

About BeyondSpring
BeyondSpring (NASDAQ: BYSI) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class therapies for cancers with high unmet needs. Its lead asset, Plinabulin, has been studied in more than 700 cancer patients and is in late-stage development across multiple cancer indications. Plinabulin’s novel mechanism as a GEF-H1 agonist with dendritic cell maturation benefit supports both anticancer activity and immune modulation, offering a unique approach to resensitizing tumors that have progressed on checkpoint inhibitors. In addition, it has the potential to synergize with chemotherapy, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), radiation, and checkpoint inhibitors. BeyondSpring is also an early incubator of and maintains an equity interest in SEED Therapeutics, a clinical-stage targeted protein degradation molecular glue company with investments from Eli Lilly and Eisai. Learn more at beyondspringpharma.com.

About Plinabulin and the Clinical Rationale for the DUBLIN-4 Trial
Plinabulin is a late-stage, first-in-class investigational GEF-H1 agonist with a differentiated mechanism of action that includes dendritic cell maturation, anti-angiogenic activity and mitigation of chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. To date, more than 700 cancer patients have been treated with Plinabulin across multiple clinical programs in various cancer types, demonstrating an extensive clinical safety database.

The post-ICI setting remains difficult to treat: 12 Phase 3 trials evaluating different treatment approaches against docetaxel, including four involving ADCs, have failed to demonstrate an overall survival benefit over docetaxel.

In the Phase 3 DUBLIN-3 trial, published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine in 2024, Plinabulin combined with docetaxel demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in OS in second- and third-line EGFR wild-type NSCLC vs. docetaxel alone (n=559), showing superior OS benefit in non-squamous patients (n=332, OS HR 0.72, p=0.0078). The combination also demonstrated statistically significant improvements compared to docetaxel alone, including doubling the 2-year and 3-year survival rates and improvements in PFS and ORR, while also significantly reducing grade 4 neutropenia (p<0.0001).

Importantly, a post hoc analysis of the DUBLIN-3 post-ICI subgroup showed a median OS of 15.8 months with Plinabulin plus docetaxel versus 11.7 months with docetaxel alone (HR 0.55), with ORR of 18.2% versus 8.0%, respectively. These findings support the clinical rationale for Plinabulin’s differentiated dendritic cell maturation mechanism and its further evaluation in DUBLIN-4.

This rationale was further supported by prospective data from the Phase 2 Study 303 (n=47), presented at ASCO 2026. In patients with NSCLC whose disease had progressed following PD-1 inhibitor treatment, the combination of Plinabulin, docetaxel and a PD-1 inhibitor demonstrated encouraging anticancer activity. With a median follow-up of 28.8 months, the Plinabulin combination showed a median PFS of 7.0 months, a disease control rate of 79.5%, and a confirmed ORR of 18.2%, with a 2-year OS rate of 58%, nearly double the historical rate reported with docetaxel in a similar patient population.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Trinity Place Holdings Inc. (OTC PINK: TPHS) (the "Company," "we," "our," or "us") today announced operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

The Company is an intellectual property holding, investment, and commercialization company. We own and control a portfolio of intellectual property assets focused on the consumer sector, a legacy of our predecessor, Syms Corp. (“Syms”), including FilenesBasement.com, as well as the intellectual property associated with the Running of the Brides® event and the An Educated Consumer is Our Best Customer® slogan. Our strategy today centers on monetizing these assets through brand licensing, e-commerce initiatives, strategic partnerships, and protection and enforcement of our intellectual property rights.

Net Operating Losses

At September 30, 2026, the Company had carryforwards of federal net operating losses (“NOLs”) of approximately $352.8 million available to reduce future federal taxes. Of the Company’s federal NOLs, $224.5 million were generated prior to 2018 and may expire if unused by 2037, and $128.2 million were generated in 2018 and later years and can be carried forward indefinitely subject to an 80 percent taxable income annual limitation.

Based on management’s assessment, it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets associated with the federal NOLs will not be realized by future taxable income or tax planning strategies. Accordingly, the Company has a valuation allowance of $74.1 million as of September 30, 2026. If our assumptions change and we determine that we will be able to realize these federal NOLs, the tax benefits relating to any reversal of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets would be recognized as a reduction of income tax expense and an increase in the deferred tax asset.

Note that our certificate of incorporation includes a provision intended to help preserve certain tax benefits primarily associated with our NOLs. This provision generally prohibits, subject to certain exceptions, transfers of stock that would result in a person or group of persons becoming a 4.75 percent stockholder, or that would result in an increase or decrease in stock ownership by a person or group of persons that is an existing 4.75 percent stockholder.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 13, 2026) - NuGen Medical Devices Inc. (TSXV: NGMD) ("NuGen" or the "Company"), a developer of needle-free drug delivery technology, provides an update regarding its Canadian medical device licence for the InsuJet™ needle-free insulin injection system.

Further to the Company's news release dated February 5, 2026, Health Canada has issued a Notice of Refusal in respect of the Company's Class II medical device licence application no. 407982. As previously disclosed, the Company's prior Canadian medical device licence had lapsed and sales in Canada were halted while the new application was under review. Sales and further supply of InsuJet in Canada remain halted.

Health Canada determined that the clinical evidence submitted with the application was insufficient to demonstrate compliance with certain safety and effectiveness requirements under sections 11, 12 and 13 of the Canadian Medical Devices Regulations. The matters identified by Health Canada include the need for additional evidence concerning insulin-specific clinical performance, bioequivalence or alternatively evidence supporting the safety and effectiveness of insulin therapy using the device, longer-term glycemic control and safety endpoints, reliable patient self-administration, and injection performance.

The Notice of Refusal applies to the Canadian application and does not, by itself, amend the regulatory status of InsuJet in jurisdictions outside Canada. NuGen continues to maintain registrations and commercial activities in a number of markets outside Canada, subject in each case to applicable local regulatory requirements.

The Notice of Refusal does not state that InsuJet is unsafe or ineffective. It states that the evidence submitted was insufficient to demonstrate that the requirements applicable to the Canadian application and its proposed use with NovoRapid insulin had been met. Investors should not interpret this distinction as an assurance that a future Canadian application will be approved.

Canadian Market and Existing Users

Based on discussions with the Company's Canadian regulatory representative, the Notice of Refusal does not require a recall of InsuJet devices previously lawfully imported and sold in Canada while the applicable licence was active. The Company has also been advised that existing Canadian users are not required to discontinue use of devices already supplied.

Clinical Evidence and Regulatory Path Forward

NuGen intends to review the Notice of Refusal with its regulatory and clinical advisers and to continue discussions with Health Canada concerning the evidence that may be required for a future submission. Subject to available funding, final protocol design, regulatory feedback and other factors, the Company currently intends to incorporate relevant elements of Health Canada's feedback into clinical evidence-generation activities in connection with its next-generation needle-free injector platform.

Management Comment

"We are disappointed with Health Canada's decision, but the Notice of Refusal provides greater clarity regarding the additional clinical evidence required for a future Canadian application," said Liang Lin, Chief Executive Officer of NuGen. "We intend to consider these requirements as part of our planned clinical program for our next-generation needle-free technology. While sales and further supply in Canada remain halted, we remain committed to working with our regulatory and clinical partners to address Health Canada's requirements and pursue a path back to the Canadian market."

About NuGen Medical Devices

NuGen develops next-generation needle-free devices for subcutaneous drug delivery. Its flagship InsuJet™ system has been registered in numerous international markets and is designed to provide an alternative to conventional needle-based injections.

HOUSTON, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cerenome, Inc. (Nasdaq: CNSY) (“Cerenome” or the “Company”), a CNS oncology company advancing an integrated platform that combines precision diagnostics, targeted radiopharmaceuticals, and artificial intelligence, announces financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provides an overview of recent business progress.

“Recognition of our first quarter of CNSide® diagnostic revenue and commercial payments beginning in October is a tremendous landmark,” said Marc H. Hedrick, M.D., Cerenome’s President and Chief Executive Officer. “Furthermore, our payer universe continues to expand with now about 80% of U.S. private payers representing approximately 190 million covered lives. Most recently, with Aetna coverage, it gives physicians an in-network option for both tumor cell enumeration and molecular profiling. In parallel, our growing commercial team is focused on helping more cancer centers use our test in patient care. In therapeutics, we materially advanced our two key programs by completing enrollment in our Phase 2 trial in adults with recurrent glioblastoma, opening up higher dose cohorts in the repeat dosing of REYOBIQ™ in patients with leptomeningeal metastases and reporting interim data in that trial.”

Q3 2026 AND RECENT HIGHLIGHTS

Corporate

  • During the quarter, Plus Therapeutics rebranded as Cerenome, and on August 3 its common stock began trading on Nasdaq under the symbol CNSY. The new name and brand reflect the Company’s focus on integrating CNS diagnostics, therapeutics, and data.
  • In November, Ron Andrews was appointed as Chief Business Officer to advance CNSide commercial adoption and strategic partnerships. Mr. Andrews continues to serve on the Company’s Board of Directors.

CNSide® CSF Assay Platform

  • The company submitted billing claims for approximately $1.55 million in gross billings at list prices and recognized $0.7 million in net diagnostic revenue in the quarter after estimated payer adjustments and price concessions.
  • Contracted coverage was expanded through agreements with Medical Mutual, Health Care Service Corporation and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan.
  • Secured in-network agreements were also made with Florida Blue and Aetna. The Aetna agreement, effective November 1, is the first national CNSide payer agreement to include both tumor cell enumeration and molecular profiling. The Company’s aggregate contracted footprint now represents approximately 190 million covered lives.
  • The company entered into a collaboration with Genomic Testing Cooperative to add DNA and RNA profiling to CNSide. In July, the Company also highlighted updated NCCN CNS Cancers Guidelines recognizing a role for CSF analysis in the assessment of LM.
  • XiFin was selected for revenue cycle management and clearinghouse services, and Samantha Fowlkes was appointed as Vice President and Head of Commercial Sales for CNSide Diagnostics.
  • The Company is on track for Medicare reimbursement in 1st half of 2027 and is separately pursuing a coverage determination from Novitas Solutions.
  • CNSide CSF Molecular Profile tests were launched for solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. The test was available to order beginning October 12, providing DNA and RNA profiling from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). CNSide can be ordered independently or alongside tumor cell enumeration.

REYOBIQ™ Development

  • The company presented interim Phase 1 ReSPECT-LM (multi-dose) findings at the Society of Neuro Oncology Annual meeting in November. The first 10 patients have been treated with repeated intraventricular doses of REYOBIQ, with no dose-limiting toxicities or treatment discontinuations due to adverse events reported. This highlights the potential for REYOBIQ to safely administer higher dose of tumor-destroying radiation (compared to single-dose study). Dose escalation is ongoing to identify a recommended multiple-dose regimen for a follow-on randomized study.
  • Also, enrollment was completed in the Phase 2 ReSPECT-GBM study in recurrent glioblastoma in October. Cerenome expects topline data in mid-2027 following additional patient follow-up, and plans to hold an End-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA thereafter.
  • Investigators reported preclinical data at the Rivkin Ovarian Cancer Research Symposium in October showing the active agent in REYOBIQ was associated with a new mechanism of action, namely positively impacting the tumor environment. The net effect described by investigators was administering REYOBIQ along with anti-PD-1 checkpoint blockade enhanced antitumor activity in these preclinical studies, opening up the possibility of novel combination therapies.
  • Investigators presented pharmacokinetic, dosimetry, and safety observations from the ReSPECT-LM program at the SNO/ASCO CNS Metastases Conference in August. A separate presentation examined the potential health economic impact of earlier detection of leptomeningeal metastases (LM) using CNSide.

THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS

  • Cash, cash equivalents and investments totaled $4.9 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with $8.6 million as of June 30, 2026. In September, the Company announced closing a senior secured financing facility up to $20 million with royalty-based repayments. In addition, the Company raised $3.8M under the Equity Distribution Agreement subsequent to the end of the quarter.
  • Total revenue was $0.7 million, consisting entirely of net diagnostic revenue.
  • Cost of revenue was $0.9 million. Research and development expense was $2.1 million, compared with $2.4 million a year earlier. Selling, general and administrative expense was $5.2 million, compared with $3.4 million a year earlier.
  • Operating loss was $7.5 million, compared with $4.5 million a year earlier. Net loss was $8.7 million, or $1.14 per share, compared with $4.4 million, or $1.03 per share, a year earlier.

ANTICIPATED MILESTONES AND OUTLOOK FOR 2027

CNSide Commercial Rollout

  • Expand CNSide adoption across cancer centers, build-out the field sales team, enhance the testing menu and build on existing payer collection experience across the CNSide test menu.

REYOBIQ Clinical Program

  • Continue dose escalation in LM Multi-dose study and follow patients in ReSPECT-GBM for the anticipated mid-2027 topline readouts from both trials.

Conference Call and Webcast
Cerenome will host a conference call and webcast Monday, November 16, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time to discuss third quarter results and provide a business update.

Webcast and Conference Call
Date/Time: Monday, November 16, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET
Webcast: https://event.choruscall.com/mediaframe/webcast.html?webcastid=vTAb1pUs
Dial-in: U.S.: 833-862-0853
International: 412-317-6789
  Please dial in 15 minutes before the start time.
   

Following the live call, a replay will be available on the Company’s website under the ‘For Investors’ section. The webcast will be available on the Company’s website for 90 days following the live call.

About Leptomeningeal metastases (LM)
Leptomeningeal metastases (LM) are a rare but severe complication of advanced cancer, affecting the fluid-lined structures of the central nervous system. LM occurs in approximately 5% of patients with metastatic cancer, with breast cancer, lung cancer, and melanoma being the most common sources. Median survival is typically 2-6 months, and effective treatment options are limited, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapies.

About REYOBIQ™ (rhenium Re186 obisbemeda)
REYOBIQ (rhenium Re186 obisbemeda) is a novel injectable radiotherapy specifically formulated to deliver direct targeted high-dose radiation in CNS tumors in a safe, effective, and convenient manner to optimize patient outcomes. REYOBIQ has the potential to reduce off-target risks and improve outcomes for CNS cancer patients versus currently approved therapies, with a more targeted and potent radiation dose. Rhenium-186 is an ideal radioisotope for CNS therapeutic applications due to its short half-life, beta energy for destroying cancerous tissue, and gamma energy for real-time imaging. REYOBIQ is being evaluated for the treatment of recurrent glioblastoma, leptomeningeal metastases, and pediatric brain cancer in the ReSPECT-GBM, ReSPECT-LM, and ReSPECT-PBC clinical trials, respectively. ReSPECT-GBM is supported by an award from the National Cancer Institute (NCI), part of the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH), and ReSPECT-LM is funded by a three-year $17.6 million grant from the Cancer Prevention & Research Institute of Texas (CPRIT). The Company's ReSPECT-PBC clinical trial for pediatric brain cancer is supported by a $3 million grant from the U.S. Department of Defense's Peer Reviewed Cancer Research Program.

About CNSide Diagnostics, LLC
CNSide Diagnostics, LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Cerenome, Inc. that develops and commercializes proprietary laboratory-developed tests, such as CNSide®, designed to identify tumor cells that have metastasized to the central nervous system in patients with carcinomas and melanomas. The CNSide® CSF Assay Platform enables quantitative analysis of the cerebrospinal fluid that informs and improves the management of patients with leptomeningeal metastases.

About Cerenome
Cerenome (Nasdaq: CNSY) is a CNS oncology company advancing an integrated platform that combines precision diagnostics, targeted therapeutics, and artificial intelligence to improve outcomes for patients with central nervous system cancers. The CNSide® CSF diagnostics platform combines cellular and molecular testing to support the detection, characterization, and longitudinal assessment of cancers involving the CNS.

Its lead therapeutic platform, REYOBIQ™ (rhenium Re186 obisbemeda), is being evaluated in clinical trials for leptomeningeal metastases, recurrent glioblastoma, and pediatric brain cancers. The data & artificial intelligence platform is designed to integrate diagnostic, molecular, imaging, and clinical data into actionable insights that support precision oncology and therapeutic innovation.

By integrating commercial diagnostics, targeted therapeutics, proprietary longitudinal data, and artificial intelligence within a single organization, Cerenome is building a differentiated CNS oncology platform designed to improve patient care while creating long-term shareholder value. (the “Company” or “CLC”) (CSE: CLC) (OTCQB: CLCFF) (FRANKFURT: CLB) announces that its Board of Directors has appointed Nicco Dehaan, the Company’s co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, as Chief Executive Officer, effective November 13, 2026. Mr. Dehaan succeeds Mark Aiken, who is moving on to pursue other opportunities.

The appointment follows the Board’s decision, announced November 10, 2026, that CLC will remain independent and pursue its standalone plan: a sharper focus on the cultivation and sale of cannabis flower, lower costs, increased cultivation capacity and continued debt repayment. With that plan centred on CLC’s farms, the Board believes the Company is best led by the executive who built and runs them.

Mr. Dehaan co-founded CLC and has served as a director since 2019. As COO and Master Grower, he has overseen cultivation, processing and production across the Company’s Christina Lake and Midway properties and has worked closely on sales and product strategy. He will continue to serve as Chief Operating Officer and as a director.

“Having chosen to remain independent, our priority now is execution – getting the most out of the land, facilities and people we already have,” said Jay McMillan, Chairman of the Board. “Nicco knows this business from the ground up. He helped build it, and he led the operations behind our strong harvest this year. He is the right person to take CLC into its next phase. On behalf of the Board, I thank Mark for his leadership over the past four years, and wish him every success.”

“I’m proud to lead the company I helped found,” said Mr. Dehaan. “We have excellent land, proven infrastructure and a team that delivered a strong harvest this year. My priorities are clear: grow more high-quality flower from the assets we already own, keep costs down, continue paying down debt and build value for our shareholders. I look forward to working with our team and the Board to get it done.”

About Christina Lake Cannabis Corp.

CLC is a licensed producer of cannabis under the Cannabis Act (Canada) with a standard cultivation licence and corresponding processing amendment from Health Canada as well as a research and development licence. "Perpetua made significant progress in Q3 2026," said Jon Cherry, President and CEO of Perpetua Resources. "From advancing temporary and permanent worker housing to pioneering new access into the site, our Stibnite Gold Project is well positioned to move forward with disciplined execution. Our exploration drill program delivered compelling new mineralization, including multiple high-grade gold intervals and a new gold-tungsten discovery."

Webinar Update on Tuesday, November 17, 2026

Perpetua is pleased to announce that it will host a webinar on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 9:00 AM Mountain Time (11:00 AM Eastern Time). The webinar will feature members of the executive team and provide an update on project construction and a summary of recent exploration results. The presentation will be followed by a question & answer session. Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights

  • Construction: Worker housing facility civil works were completed in late August 2026, and foundation installation commenced during the quarter. Work on the Burntlog Route ramped up through the summer field season, and long-lead powerline items have been ordered.
  • Exploration: The 2026 Exploration Drilling Program is complete, with more than 16,000 meters of core drilled. In August and then in November 2026, the Company reported new high-grade gold and antimony discoveries and identified a new gold-tungsten zone.
  • Financing update: Perpetua continued diligence and documentation on the $2.9 billion senior secured long-term loan from the Export-Import Bank of the United States ("U.S. EXIM") under the Make More in America Initiative, approved by the U.S. EXIM board on May 21, 2026. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027. The Company continues to advance detailed engineering, long-lead procurement, early works, critical path construction, and execution planning ahead of a final investment and construction decision. Unrestricted cash was $443.4 million as of September 30, 2026.
  • Antimony pilot plant: In July 2026, the Company commissioned a mobile modular processing plant, in partnership with Idaho National Laboratory, for pilot-scale testing to advance a secure domestic supply chain for antimony trisulfide.
  • Community: In July 2026, the Company opened a community resource and visitor information center in Yellow Pine, Idaho.

Construction Update

Perpetua completed 494,480 work hours during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with no reportable spills and no serious injuries. Other highlights include:

  • Burntlog Route: Crews advanced construction along the alignment, removed dead timber left by past wildfires, and moved to pioneer roadwork. The year-round access road will give the Project an expanded and upgraded route capable of handling larger loads and equipment.
  • Worker Housing Facility: Treated wood foundations were installed for the kitchen, dining, and recreation modules, and a metal foundation was installed to support the dormitory buildings and the arctic corridor.
  • Powerline: Perpetua is well advanced in procuring key equipment. Substations and transformers are on order, while deliveries of power poles and ancillary equipment continue to the Company's laydown areas in Donnelly and Cascade, Idaho. Power pole installation commenced in October.

Looking ahead, Perpetua will continue to advance critical path work including bridge deliveries for Burntlog Route, installation of the worker housing facility, ongoing powerline procurement and construction, and placing orders for long-lead-time equipment.

New Exploration Results Announced

The 2026 drilling program sought to upgrade in-pit and near-pit inferred resources, extend mineralization along strike, test key underground targets, and follow up on discoveries from the 2025-2026 program. Recent highlights included:

  • Fiddle Discovery: The new Fiddle prospect, located approximately 750 meters south of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit, includes some of the most significant mineralized material encountered at the Stibnite Gold Project to date. Discovery hole SB633 returned 109.7 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 1.1% antimony. Fiddle adds a new target area with potential to expand the Project's in-pit and near-pit resource base. The Company has since completed significant additional drilling at Fiddle, with assay results expected in the coming months.
  • Clark Tunnel Fault Zone (CTFZ): First announced in August, the CTFZ is located within or adjacent to the southeastern limits of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit. New results announced earlier this month returned near-surface, high-grade gold intercepts from recent drilling, including 25.4 meters of 4.5 g/t gold from 13 meters downhole and 25.0 meters of 2.3 g/t gold from 18 meters downhole. These results follow the drilling announced in August, which included a tungsten discovery in Hole SB597 that returned 21.3 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 0.9% tungsten from 24 meters downhole.

Near-Term Outlook

Through the remainder of 2026 and early 2027, Perpetua is advancing early works, critical path construction, and detailed engineering for the process plant. Other initiatives include finalizing key construction and equipment contracts. With the 2026 exploration program recently completed, Perpetua expects to announce ongoing exploration results into 2027.

Website: www.perpetuaresources.com

About Perpetua Resources and the Stibnite Gold Project
Perpetua Resources Corp., through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is focused on the exploration, site restoration and redevelopment of gold-antimony-silver deposits in the Stibnite-Yellow Pine district of central Idaho. The Stibnite Gold Project is one of the highest-grade, open-pit gold deposits in the United States and holds the only identified domestic reserve of the critical mineral antimony, which is essential to the defense, energy and manufacturing sectors. The Project is designed to apply a modern, responsible mining approach to restore a historic mine site and provide uplift to water quality, improve fish habitat access, and invest in river restoration while supporting local economic development in rural Idaho.

TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Organigram Global Inc. If the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, it may be eligible for an additional 180-calendar-day compliance period, subject to satisfying applicable Nasdaq requirements, including transferring its listing to the Nasdaq Capital Market. HOUSTON, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- First Horizon Bank (NYSE: FHN) (or "First Horizon") today announced it is working alongside Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston and AltCap to implement an innovative financing solution to build a new 60,000-square-foot facility that will significantly improve access to food and other services for low-income Houstonians. The new Family Opportunity Center in north Houston will leverage New Markets Tax Credits (NMTC) provided by First Horizon Bank and the Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) AltCap.

Slated to open its doors in 2028, the Family Opportunity Center will feature a market-style food pantry, thrift store, and access to the nonprofit's services, including mental health counseling, parenting classes, rental assistance and job readiness resources. It will also provide space for community and first responders during natural disasters, along with ample warehouse space for food storage.

The total investment for the center, located at 9111 Jensen Drive, is $25 million. To date, Catholic Charities has raised $17.5 million in private and foundation gifts. The NMTC represents nearly 10 percent of the total needed.

Congress established the NMTC to encourage private-sector investment in low-income communities, including the future location of the Family Opportunity Center. Under the program, CDFIs such as AltCap are awarded tax credit allocations from the U.S. Department of the Treasury and deploy them to support projects that deliver measurable community benefits. Investors, including financial institutions like First Horizon Bank, receive federal tax credits in exchange for qualified investments. This investment structure enables community-serving projects, such as the Family Opportunity Center, to access favorable financing and move forward when traditional financing alone may be insufficient.

"We are proud to work alongside Catholic Charities and AltCap to provide financing for the Family Opportunity Center," said Yasmin Huebinger, Houston Commercial Banking Leader for First Horizon Bank. "This investment reflects First Horizon's commitment to strengthening the communities we serve, expanding economic opportunities and driving sustainable growth that benefits families and the broader Houston community."

"As Catholic Charities continues its Building to Serve Capital Campaign, the Family Opportunity Center stands as a testament to what can be achieved when nonprofit organizations, community development partners and financial institutions align resources around a shared vision," said Michael D. Hansen, president and CEO of Catholic Charities. "The cooperation among Catholic Charities, AltCap and First Horizon Bank illustrates how innovative financing can help transform lives and strengthen communities across the Houston region."

"As a CDFI that has been helping to increase access to capital for Houston entrepreneurs and small businesses since 2022, AltCap is excited to demonstrate how we can also support high impact community investments like the Family Opportunity Center using the NMTC Program," said Ruben Alonso III, CEO of AltCap. "We look forward to continuing to bring capital and other resources to underserved communities and small businesses throughout Houston as well as Harris County." 

The Catholic Charities Family Opportunity Center is AltCap's first NMTC investment in Texas. ROCHESTER, NEW YORK, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Syntec Optics Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: OPTX) (“Syntec Optics” or the “Company”), a provider of deep-tech products to industry pioneers connecting and protecting the world, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Supporting mission-critical applications ranging from low-Earth-orbit satellites and bipartisan connected-battlefield defense platforms to life sciences, Syntec delivered an all-time high revenue of $8.5 million, up 23% year over year, and net income improved by $1.6 million to a positive net income of $0.2 million, compared with a $1.4 million net loss in the prior-year quarter. The quarter’s results reflect Syntec’s expanding role in next-generation bipartisan defense and space technologies, including continued growth in major programs of national importance like Artemis III, low-Earth orbit reconnaissance, satellite collision-avoidance, and AR/VR soldier gear. Syntec combined these achievements with lower selling, general, and administrative expenses. Overall cash reserves strengthened, growing by $0.3 million.

Earnings Call information:

Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026

Time: 5:00 p.m. ET

Register in Advance (Required): https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/wUCh5icdSQm20ccy7aOSoA

(After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information about joining the meeting.)

Webcast: A recording of the conference call will be available under the Latest Events section on the Investors page of Syntec Optics’ website at www.syntecoptics.com.

Replay: A replay of the webcast will be available approximately three hours after the call concludes. It will remain accessible until Tuesday, December 1, 2026, in the Investor Relations section of Syntec Optics’ website at www.syntecoptics.com.

"We are excited to be moving quickly with a well-disciplined execution plan, adding proven pioneering programs to existing customer products, all typical with a 7-10 year product life cycle and needing replacement over time," said Matt Carey, Vice President of Business Development.

Gross profit for the quarter increased 127% year over year to $1.9 million. Gross margin nearly doubled compared with the prior-year quarter. Selling, general, and administrative expenses were $1.7 million, reduced by $0.3 million from the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was $0.9 million, or 10% of revenue, compared with approximately break-even and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of nearly 0% in the prior-year quarter. 

Beginning this quarter, we are presenting revenue across five end markets: Space Tech, Defense Tech, Life Sciences, AI Data Center, and Other Scientific Instruments. These categories will provide greater visibility into the markets served by our products and the demand drivers affecting our business going forward. Space Tech includes space-related communications, orbital safety, reconnaissance, and rockets. Defense Tech covers bipartisan, cross-administration, proven next-gen AI-driven AR/VR connected battlefield, night-vision, and other soldier gear. Together, Space Tech and Defense Tech represent 64% of our third-quarter revenues and are expected to continue driving our success in subsequent quarters.

Our fastest-growing end market is space technology. Syntec is excited to share that Space Tech revenue increased 117% year over year to $1.3 million. In Q3, Space Tech represented 15% of quarterly revenue and was the fastest-growing segment for the quarter. Our space products support low-Earth-orbiting satellites, debris detection and collision avoidance, reconnaissance, and lunar rocket hardware. In Q3, we announced orders that expand our participation in orbital safety and government satellite reconnaissance. These new product lines broaden our space business across multiple customer programs and mission requirements.

After quarter-end, we announced orders for a new program for our actuator products to support NASA’s Artemis III rockets. This program extends our space portfolio from satellites into hardware supporting lunar missions.

Defense Tech revenues increased 31% year over year to $4.2 million. This represents 49% of quarterly revenue. Our products support AI-enabled AR/VR soldier systems, night vision, missile guidance, and laser targeting products. Announcements during the year included camera and display-window products for military wearable systems, demonstrating expanded participation in customer platforms. Growth across established and newer applications supports our focus on supplying mission-critical products throughout customer program life cycles.

Our Life Sciences revenue increased 12% year over year to $2.7 million, representing 31% of quarterly revenue. Our product lines in this market serve blood diagnostics for early detection of disease, biomedical illumination and visualization, surgical robotics, DNA sequencing, ophthalmology, and veterinary care. These programs provide a substantial revenue base alongside our expanding defense and space base, giving Syntec a more diverse product mix.

AI Data Center revenue was $0.2 million. We expect this category to grow in the coming years as our products are deployed across multiple value chains within the data center. Activities include precision micro-connectors for transceivers and photonic integrated circuits, as well as optics supporting emerging orbital and earth-based fusion energy. A massive energy shortage is predicted by nearly all analysts, and Syntec plans to participate in next-generation products with cutting-edge pioneers. In August, we reported approximately $4.0 million in cumulative orders across the broader AI infrastructure “picks and shovels” opportunity since entering that market roughly two years ago.

Other scientific instruments revenue, which includes products for quantum computing applications, was $0.2 million.

The Company ended the quarter with $14.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, up from $14.0 million at the end of the second quarter. Operating activities generated $1.3 million of cash during the first nine months of the year.  “Our strong cash position gives us the flexibility to invest alongside our customers as their next-generation technologies ramp up to high production volumes for 7-10 year product life cycles,” said Dean Rudy, Chief Financial Officer. “We see an opportunity to build on our momentum in defense and space by expanding our manufacturing capabilities, utilizing our open capacity, and pursuing complementary growth opportunities. Our focus is on translating that opportunity into sustained revenue growth and stronger profitability.”

In the fourth quarter and beyond, the company continues to add new programs to utilize our open capacity for long product life cycles. 

About Syntec Optics

Headquartered in Rochester, N.Y., Syntec Optics Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: OPTX) is one of the nation’s largest bespoke makers of high-precision optics. It pushes the limits of light-based technologies to connect and protect the world. Syntec supports critical missions ranging from low-Earth-orbit satellites to advanced next-gen connected-battlefield defense platforms, moon rocket actuators, AI data centers, and life sciences. As light-enabled technologies continue to account for a significant portion of global economic output—representing nearly $20 trillion of the $111 trillion in total worldwide production as of 2024—Syntec Optics remains positioned at the forefront of the modern optical revolution.

VANCOUVER, BC and GLIL YAM, Israel, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IM Cannabis Corp. (the "Company") (NASDAQ: IMCC) announced its financial results for the third quarter and first nine months ended September 30, 2026.

For the third quarter of 2026, revenue totaled C$1.65 million, compared to C$5.08 million in the same period last year. The Company reported a gross loss of C$35,000 and a total net loss of C$7.08 million, compared to a net loss of C$3.87 million in the third quarter of 2025. For the first nine months of 2026, revenue totaled C$8.96 million, compared to C$15.77 million in the corresponding period of 2025, while total net loss amounted to C$13.93 million, compared to C$3.88 million.

In September 2026, the Company announced a non-binding agreement to acquire a 51% stake in Space Defense Innovations LLC (SDI), a Polish company operating in the unmanned aerial systems sector through its subsidiary BlueAero Group, which distributes tactical UAS products manufactured by BlueBird Aero Systems. The Company is currently negotiating a definitive share purchase agreement with SDI's shareholders.

Separately, the Company completed the sale of its European-focused operations, including its German subsidiary Adjupharm GmbH, to Slil.com Holding Ltd. on September 29, 2026, following a restructuring under which the Company's Israeli medical cannabis operations were retained. The transaction consideration included a C$3 million advance payment and the assumption of certain liabilities of up to C$9.4 million. The Company expects the transaction to improve shareholders' equity by approximately C$3 million.

The full Interim Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis are available on SEDAR+ and EDGAR.

About IM Cannabis Corp.

IM Cannabis Corp. (NASDAQ: IMCC) is an international company operating a medical cannabis platform serving patients in Israel.

The Company's ecosystem operates in Israel through its subsidiaries, which import and distribute cannabis to medical patients, leveraging years of proprietary data and patient insights. The Company also operates medical cannabis retail pharmacies and online platforms in Israel that enable the safe delivery and quality control of IMCC's products throughout the value chain.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / Core Critical Metals Corp. ("CCMC" or the "Company") (TSXV:CCMC)(OTCQB:CCMCF) is pleased to announce a non-brokered private placement of up to 1,000,000 flow-through common shares of the Company (each, an "FT Share") at a price of $0.50 per FT Share for gross proceeds of up to $500,000 (the "Offering"). The FT Shares will be offered by way of private placement pursuant to available exemptions from the prospectus requirements under applicable securities laws.

Each FT Share will be issued as a "flow-through share" within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the "Tax Act"). The gross proceeds from the Offering will be used to incur Canadian exploration expenses that qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" under the Tax Act and, where applicable, as "BC flow-through mining expenditures" under the Income Tax Act (British Columbia), on the Company's LMSL (Lucky Mike - Silver Lode) copper-molybdenum-tungsten project near Merritt, British Columbia. The Company will renounce such expenditures to subscribers with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026, and will incur such expenditures on or before December 31, 2027.

No finder's fees are payable in connection with the Offering, and no insiders of the Company will participate in the Offering.

Closing of the Offering is subject to receipt of all necessary approvals, including the acceptance of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV"). All securities issued under the Offering will be subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance in accordance with applicable securities laws and the policies of the TSXV.

About Core Critical Metals Corp.

Core Critical Metals Corp. is a North American mineral acquisition and exploration company focused on the development of quality critical metal properties with high-upside and expansion potential. Its principal project is the LMSL (Lucky Mike - Silver Lode) copper-molybdenum-tungsten project near Merritt, British Columbia.
